fatal_errors: The hypothesis treats machine learning as a surface-modification method, although it is only a possible design or optimization tool and does not physically modify stainless steel.
It fails to identify the central intervention: atmospheric plasma spraying of an AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating followed by annealing at 550 °C for 2 h.
It provides no material-specific mechanism involving grain refinement, BCC/FCC phase structure, sluggish diffusion, or protective Al- and Cr-rich passive oxides.
It omits the relevant electrochemical and molten-salt exposure conditions and supplies no supporting evidence.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad objective of improving stainless-steel corrosion resistance and proposes a basic modified-versus-unmodified corrosion test. However, it does not reconstruct the reported coating and annealing method, its operating conditions, structural mediators, corrosion mechanism, quantitative outcomes, or qualified boundaries. The proposed machine-learning intervention is underspecified and scientifically incomplete because model predictions alone cannot alter a surface. Its falsification experiment is directionally usable but does not define the physical treatment selected by the model, exposure chemistry, controls, or electrochemical and hot-corrosion measurements needed to test the target claims.
